content.content:
# Cardio App

A Flutter heart health companion app with real-time 3-lead ECG monitoring, AI-powered cardiac classification, and fall detection.

## Tech Stack
- Flutter (Dart SDK >=3.10.8 <4.0.0)
- Firebase Core, Firebase Auth, Cloud Firestore
- Running on **Android** (BLE requires native platform)
- Firebase project: `cardio-app-d4c55`
- fl_chart: ^0.70.2 (real-time ECG waveform visualization)
- flutter_blue_plus: ^1.35.0 (BLE communication with ESP32)
- permission_handler: ^11.0.0 (runtime BLE/location permissions)
- google_sign_in: ^6.2.1 (Google OAuth sign-in)
- tflite_flutter: ^0.12.1 (on-device AI inference for ECG + fall detection)
- flutter_local_notifications: ^19.0.0 (push alerts for abnormal ECG)
- google_fonts: ^6.0.0 (Inter font)
- shared_preferences: ^2.3.0 (local alert history)

## Hardware
- **Device**: ESP32 microcontroller
- **ECG**: 3-lead ECG module (e.g., AD8232) on PCB
- **Connection**: BLE (Bluetooth Low Energy)
- **Output**: JSON over BLE notifications
- **Sampling Rate**: ~250 Hz
- **ADC Resolution**: 12-bit (0-4095)

## Project Structure
```
lib/
├── main.dart                     # Firebase init + dark theme + MaterialApp
├── firebase_options.dart         # FlutterFire CLI generated
├── core/
│   ├── app_shell.dart            # Bottom nav (Monitor, History, Profile) + service ownership
│   └── splash_screen.dart        # Animated splash → auth check → routing
└── features/
    ├── auth/
    │   ├── data/
    │   │   ├── auth_service.dart        # Firebase Auth + Firestore wrapper
    │   │   └── user_model.dart          # UserModel with profile fields
    │   └── presentation/
    │       ├── login_page.dart
    │       ├── signup_page.dart
    │       └── forgot_password_page.dart
    ├── bluetooth/
    │   └── data/
    │       ├── ble_service.dart          # ESP32 BLE: scan, connect, parse JSON ECG batches
    │       ├── ecg_data_model.dart       # EcgSample (3 ADC values) + EcgPrediction (5-class)
    │       └── sensor_data_model.dart    # SensorData + Vec3 (for fall detection BLE data)
    ├── ecg/
    │   └── data/
    │       ├── ecg_processor.dart        # Real-time DSP: ADC→mV, baseline removal, z-score normalize
    │       ├── ecg_inference_service.dart # TFLite ECG model + EMA smoothing + prediction stream
    │       └── notification_service.dart  # Local push notifications on abnormal ECG
    ├── fall_detection/
    │   ├── data/
    │   │   ├── fall_detection_service.dart  # TFLite fall CNN: sliding window, z-score, inference
    │   │   └── test_cases.dart              # 40 test windows from BITS-2 dataset (temporary)
    │   └── presentation/
    │       └── fall_test_page.dart           # Standalone test page (Test 1 + Run All)
    ├── dashboard/
    │   └── presentation/
    │       └── ecg_monitor_page.dart    # 3 ECG charts + AI prediction card + BLE controls
    ├── history/
    │   ├── data/
    │   │   └── ecg_history_service.dart # SharedPreferences alert log (200 max)
    │   └── presentation/
    │       └── history_page.dart        # Alert history list UI
    └── profile/
        └── presentation/
            └── profile_page.dart        # User info + notification settings + sign out

assets/
├── models/
│   └── ecg_model.tflite          # ECG 5-class classifier (~746 KB)
└── fall_detection.tflite          # Fall detection binary classifier (~656 KB)

ai/                                # Python ML pipeline (NOT part of Flutter app)
├── fall_detection.tflite          # Source model file
├── fall_detection_training.ipynb  # Colab training notebook
├── model_metadata.json            # Normalization constants, threshold, metrics
├── norm_mean.npy / norm_std.npy   # Numpy normalization arrays
├── generate_test_cases.py         # Script to regenerate test_cases.dart from BITS-2
├── validate_alignment.py          # Validates Dart test data matches training pipeline
└── Dataset/                       # BITS-2 wrist-worn sensor dataset (fall + adl CSVs)

ecg_ml/                            # Python ECG ML pipeline (NOT part of Flutter app)
├── config.py                      # Central configuration
├── requirements.txt               # Python dependencies
├── train_template.py              # Complete Colab training script
├── data/                          # PTB-XL data loading
├── preprocessing/                 # Signal processing (shared logic with Dart)
├── model/                         # CNN / CNN-LSTM architectures
├── inference/                     # Real-time buffer + prediction smoother
├── export/                        # PyTorch → ONNX → TFLite export
└── esp32_reference.md             # ESP32 wiring + Arduino sketch
```

## Architecture Decisions
- **Feature-based folder structure**: each feature has `data/` and `presentation/` subdirectories
- **AppShell** owns all shared services (BLE, ECG inference, notifications, history) and passes them to child pages
- **3-tab bottom nav**: Monitor (ECG), History (alerts), Profile (settings)
- **AuthService** centralizes all Firebase Auth + Firestore calls — pages don't call Firebase directly
- **Google Sign-In (OAuth)**: creates Firebase credential + auto-creates Firestore profile
- **BLE-only** — Classic Bluetooth was removed; uses flutter_blue_plus exclusively
- **Two AI models**: ECG classifier (5-class cardiac) + Fall detector (binary)
- **On-Device AI**: Both TFLite models run inside Flutter, NOT on ESP32
- **State management**: StatefulWidget + broadcast streams (no external state library)
- **Service injection**: prop drilling from AppShell to children

## BLE / ECG Integration
- ESP32 device name: `ECG_ESP32`
- BLE Service UUID: `12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789abc`
- BLE Characteristic UUID: `12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789abd`
- JSON batch format: `{"samples": [{"I": 2048, "II": 2100, "III": 1950}, ...]}`
- Brace-counting parser for robustness with fragmented BLE packets
- Leads-off detection: ADC values < 0 are filtered out
- Auto-reconnect on disconnect (3-second delay)
- Streams: `ecgStream` (List<EcgSample>), `connectionStream` (bool), `scanStream` (bool)

## ECG AI Pipeline
1. **Training**: PTB-XL dataset → extract 3 leads → preprocess → train in Colab
2. **Export**: PyTorch → ONNX → TFLite (float16 quantized, ~746 KB)
3. **Inference**: ECG samples → EcgProcessor (ADC→mV, baseline removal, z-score) → ring buffer (1250 samples, 3 leads) → TFLite → softmax → EMA smooth (alpha=0.3)
4. **Stride**: 250 samples (1 second) between inferences
5. **Notifications**: Local push on abnormal detection (confidence > 0.55, 30-sec cooldown per class)

## ECG Classification Classes
| Class | Full Name              | Color   |
|-------|------------------------|---------|
| NORM  | Normal ECG             | Green   |
| MI    | Myocardial Infarction  | Red     |
| STTC  | ST/T Change            | Orange  |
| CD    | Conduction Disturbance | Blue    |
| HYP   | Hypertrophy            | Purple  |

## Fall Detection (TFLite CNN)
- **Model**: Residual CNN trained on BITS-2 wrist-worn sensor dataset
- **Model file**: `assets/fall_detection.tflite` (~656 KB)
- **Input**: 128 timesteps x 12 features (9 raw sensor axes + 3 computed magnitudes)
- **Feature order**: `[acc_x, acc_y, acc_z, acg_x, acg_y, acg_z, gyro_x, gyro_y, gyro_z, acc_mag, acg_mag, gyro_mag]`
- **Normalization**: z-score with hardcoded mean/std from training (in `fall_detection_service.dart` and `ai/model_metadata.json`)
- **Sliding window**: 128 samples, step 64 (50% overlap), ~50 Hz sample rate
- **Threshold**: 0.5 probability — requires 2 consecutive windows above threshold in production
- **Test page**: Standalone `fall_test_page.dart` with 40 pre-extracted test windows (20 fall, 20 ADL)
- **Test data generation**: `ai/generate_test_cases.py` — must use EXACT same CSV parsing as training notebook (`load_and_clean_csv` with sensor pivot alignment)
- **Known**: Model v3 reports 84% sensitivity / 92% specificity on full test set
- **v4 notebook**: `ai/fall_detection_training_v4.ipynb` — improved version with SE attention, enhanced augmentation (rotation, drift, combined), adaptive labeling, cosine annealing LR, label smoothing

## Theme / Design
- **Dark theme** with Material3 (`ThemeMode.dark`)
- Background: `#0D1B2A` (near black), Surface: `#1A2332` (dark blue-gray)
- Accents: tealAccent primary + `#00BFA5` secondary
- Typography: Google Fonts (Inter)
- ECG charts: Lead I (red), Lead II (green), Lead III (blue)
- AI prediction card: color-coded by classification class
- Auth pages: teal gradient background + white text/inputs

## Navigation
```
SplashScreen (3 sec animation)
  ├→ No user → LoginPage (email/password + Google OAuth)
  └→ User exists → AppShell
                      ├── Tab 0: ECG Monitor (real-time charts + AI)
                      ├── Tab 1: History (alert log)
                      └── Tab 2: Profile (settings + sign out)
```

## Android Configuration
- minSdkVersion: 21
- Java/Kotlin: VERSION_17
- Core library desugaring enabled (`desugar_jdk_libs 2.1.4`)
- ProGuard rules for TFLite GPU delegate (`android/app/proguard-rules.pro`)
- Permissions: BLUETOOTH, BLUETOOTH_SCAN, BLUETOOTH_CONNECT, ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION

## Known Issues / Notes
- Firebase init in main.dart is wrapped in try-catch (Linux throws UnsupportedError)
- `AnimatedBuilder` is the correct Flutter widget name used in splash_screen.dart
- `sensor_data_model.dart` exists for fall detection BLE data (Vec3 accelerometer/gyroscope) — separate from ECG data model
- Fall detection test cases must be regenerated with `ai/generate_test_cases.py` if the dataset or model changes — the script uses the exact same CSV alignment as the training notebook
- ECG model must be placed at `assets/models/ecg_model.tflite`; fall model at `assets/fall_detection.tflite`
- Training code in `ecg_ml/` and `ai/` is for Google Colab — not compiled into the Flutter app
- `AuthService.createMissingProfile()` auto-creates Firestore doc for legacy users
- Notification cooldown: 30 seconds per ECG class to prevent spam

Now I have full understanding. Let me analyze the data flow:

**Tester sends:** `[0xEC, leadI_lo, leadI_hi, leadII_lo, leadII_hi, leadIII_lo, leadIII_hi, ...]` where each lead is **int16 little-endian**.

**Tester encoding:** `toAdc(val) = (2048 + val * 1000).clamp(0, 4094).toInt()` → values **0-4094** (positive ints, fits in int16). Stored via `setInt16` LE.

**Cardio app parses:** `getInt16(offset, Endian.little)` → reads back as signed int16 → **values 0-4094 (positive)**, so OK.

**Then `leadsOff` checks**: `leadI < 0 || leadII < 0 || leadIII < 0`. Since values are 0-4094, none are negative, so leadsOff is false. Good.

**Then `toMillivolts`**: assumes `vref=3.3, adcMax=4095`, midpoint `1.65V`. Then output = `((adc/4095)*3.3 - 1.65) * 1000` mV. So for adc=2048 → ~0 mV, for adc=4094 → ~1650 mV. That's ridiculously huge mV values.

Wait the tester does `toAdc(val) = 2048 + val*1000`. For the QRS peak with amplitude ~1.2 mV, val ≈ 1.2, so toAdc = 2048 + 1200 = 3248. That clamps fine.

But then the receiver converts ADC back to mV: `((3248/4095)*3.3 - 1.65)*1000` = `(0.793*3.3 - 1.65)*1000` = `(2.617 - 1.65)*1000` = `967 mV`. Way too big for ECG (should be ~1mV). But that's a *display* issue, not "no graph."

Let me re-check: the user reports `_buildPredictionCard` shows "Collecting ECG data for AI analysis..." but graph never displays. Looking at `_buildLeadChart`, when `data.isEmpty` it shows "Waiting for signal...". So if data is filling, the graph should appear.

Why would `_leadIData` stay empty? Let me re-examine **the tester service UUID and char UUID** vs cardio app ones:

Both use `0000181d-...` service and `00002a37-...` char. Match.

Wait — let me check the tester's `_payloadCapBytes = 20` (default). With samplesPerPacket = `(20-1)/6` = `19/6` = `3` samples per packet. That means each notify packet is `1 + 3*6 = 19` bytes. That's valid.

Receiver expects `value[0] == 0xEC` (header) → tester sends 0xEC ✓. Then payload `(19-1)=18 % 6 == 0` → 3 samples ✓.

So data should flow. But check the **MTU**: cardio_app requests MTU 517 after connect, but tester's `_payloadCapBytes = 20` is the default cap. The tester uses 20 bytes. After MTU negotiation, the tester probably should bump up but it stays at 20. That's still a valid notify size.

Hmm, the user says graph isn't drawn. Let me check `setState` in `_onEcgData`. It does `setState(() { ... add data... })`. Should rebuild. But the screen description says "connecting ecg data for ai analysis" - this is **the prediction card text**, "Collecting ECG data for AI analysis...". That's shown when `_prediction == null` and `(_prediction != null || _bleConnected)` — i.e., always shown when connected without prediction yet.

So the prediction card is showing but the graphs below should also show. Unless data isn't actually arriving.

Let me check — is there a chance the tester *isn't* notifying? The tester's `BlePeripheral.updateCharacteristic` sends notify only if subscribed. The `_subscribed` state is set when `setCharacteristicSubscriptionChangeCallback` fires. But the tester sends *regardless* of `_subscribed` — it just calls `updateCharacteristic`. If client isn't subscribed, those calls might fail silently or with errors but it still tries.

Now check the cardio_app subscribe call: `await characteristic.setNotifyValue(true)`. This writes to CCCD which should make tester's library register the subscription.

Let me check ecg_processor briefly to understand what happens if data is bad.

content.text:
**Found it.** On the tester (peripheral) side, the device is only added to `bluetoothDevicesMap` if it's **already bonded** at connect time. If unbonded, it triggers `createBond()` and waits — but if the central never bonds (and the cardio_app's flutter_blue_plus doesn't auto-bond), the device is never added to the map → `updateCharacteristic` finds 0 devices → notifications go nowhere.

Yet you reported "Bond: Ready". Let me see the bond completion path:

**Confirmed bug in the package:** when bond completes, it calls `gattServer.connect(device, true)` but **never adds the device to `bluetoothDevicesMap`**. So `updateCharacteristic` iterates an empty map → notifications go nowhere → "SENT" counter just counts attempts, not actual deliveries.

The fix on our side: declare the characteristic such that bonding isn't required, so the connect path goes through the `BOND_BONDED` branch (or stays unbonded but gets added). Actually looking again — in the unbonded path, the device address gets added to `listOfDevicesWaitingForBond` but never to `bluetoothDevicesMap`. Even after bonding, it still doesn't get added.

Workaround: change the characteristic permissions so they don't trigger bonding, then the device should already be `BOND_BONDED` from a prior pairing — or we use unencrypted permissions. Currently we use `AttributePermissions.readable` which shouldn't require encryption. But the issue is the connect callback still goes through the unbonded path on first connection.

Let me check if there's a simpler workaround — passing `deviceId` directly or tracking devices ourselves via `setConnectionStateChangeCallback`:

The plugin's `onConnectionStateChange` Dart callback fires for every connect. We can capture the deviceId and pass it explicitly to `updateCharacteristic`. That bypasses the empty map (no — `updateCharacteristic` still looks up by deviceId in the same broken map).

Actually look at line 190: `val device = bluetoothDevicesMap[deviceId] ?: throw Exception("Device not found")`. Same map. So both paths fail.

Real fix: pair with the cardio_app **first** (system Bluetooth settings → pair with "ECG"). Then on subsequent connects, the device's bondState is already BOND_BONDED at connect time → the `else if` branch runs → device is added to the map → notifications work.

**Try this:**
1. On the cardio_app phone, go to system Bluetooth settings.
2. Find "ECG" and pair it (it should appear while the tester is advertising).
3. Then open the cardio_app and connect.

Want me to also patch the plugin locally to fix the bond path? That would make it work without manual pairing.

content.text:
**Important finding** — at line 5 of relevant logs: `gatt_process_notification` and `bta_gattc_process_indicate no one interested, ack now`. This is **the Bluetooth stack receiving GATT indications/notifications**, but the message says **"no one interested"** — meaning notifications ARE arriving on the cardio_app phone but **no one (no Flutter app) is registered to receive them**. 

So the data IS being sent from tester to cardio_app phone via Android's BT stack, but the cardio_app's `BluetoothGatt` callback isn't registered for these notifications because subscription was never set up properly.

Now I need to find why. The cardio_app doesn't appear to be using flutter_blue_plus in these logs. Let me check the actual app process:

content.text:
**FOUND IT.** 🎯

The logs show the actual problem clearly:

```
Using fallback notifiable characteristic 2a05 from service 1801
Char 2a05: descriptors=0, hasCCCD=false, props=...indicate: true...
```

The cardio_app is subscribing to **characteristic `2a05`** in service **`1801`** — which is the standard Android **Generic Attribute Service "Service Changed"** characteristic, NOT the ECG characteristic!

The reason: cardio_app's `_findExactEcgCharacteristic` didn't find the ECG service `0000181d-...` so it fell back to `_findFirstNotifiableCharacteristic` which returned the first notifiable thing it saw — the GATT service-changed indicator.

So the tester's ECG service isn't being discovered. Looking at the BleService — service discovery returned 3 services but the ECG one (`0000181d`) wasn't among them. Either:
- The tester didn't actually publish the service, or
- `addService` ran but the discovery happened too fast (cleared cache → discoverServices ran on partially populated GATT), or  
- The advertised service UUID doesn't match the registered one.

Wait — clearGattCache! Right after we added `clearGattCache()` then `requestMtu(517)` then `discoverServices()`. The MTU was set to 512 first (Android default behavior on connect), THEN clearGattCache was called, THEN MTU 517 requested, THEN discoverServices. But `clearGattCache` invalidates the cache and the immediate `discoverServices` might catch it mid-rebuild — only finding stock GAP/GATT services.

Let me also look at the tester. Service UUID is `0000181d-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb` (Weight Scale) — odd choice. Char UUID is `00002a37-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb` (Heart Rate Measurement). These are standard SIG-defined UUIDs. Some Android peripherals reject re-registering well-known UUIDs.

But the **bigger immediate fix**: the cardio_app's "fallback to any notifiable characteristic" is harmful — it locks onto random GATT services. Remove the fallback, and add retry on missing service. Also reconsider clearGattCache timing.

Let me make these fixes:

1. Remove the fallback that subscribes to wrong characteristic.
2. Move clearGattCache to BEFORE the connect (or skip it, since flutter_blue_plus's `discoverServices` handles fresh discovery).
3. Retry service discovery if our service isn't found.

Here are the most relevant Flutter BLE peripheral / GATT server libraries for Android in 2025, based on the search results:

## Top Recommendations

### 1. **ble_peripheral** (pub.dev)
Ble peripheral is a Flutter plugin that allows you to use your device as Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) peripheral. This is an OS-independent plugin for creating a BLE Generic Attribute Profile (GATT) server to broadcast user-defined services and characteristics. This is particularly useful when prototyping and testing servers on different devices with the goal of ensuring that expected behavior matches across all systems.

Required Android permissions include BLUETOOTH, BLUETOOTH_ADMIN, BLUETOOTH_CONNECT, BLUETOOTH_ADVERTISE, and BLUETOOTH_SCAN.

### 2. **bluetooth_low_energy** / **FlutterBlePeripheral**
These are the libraries explicitly recommended by the popular `flutter_blue_plus` maintainer for peripheral role: "If you need BLE Peripheral Role, you should check out FlutterBlePeripheral, or bluetooth_low_energy."

This recommendation is significant because FlutterBluePlus supports nearly every feature on all supported platforms (iOS, macOS, Android, Linux, Web) and has zero dependencies besides Flutter, Android, iOS, and macOS themselves, which makes it very stable and easy to maintain — but it intentionally doesn't include peripheral mode, deferring to those two libraries.

### 3. **flutter_ble_peripheral_slave**
A more recently updated package (January 2026) that allows you to use your device as a BLE peripheral and creates a GATT server to broadcast user-defined services and characteristics, useful for prototyping and testing servers on different devices.

## Important Context for Choosing

According to the Exabyting BLE/GATT Flutter guide:
- Some packages are suitable for broadcasting advertisements only and do not include a built-in GATT server, so you'd have to implement a custom GATT server separately
- Other packages are good options for advertising and include a built-in GATT server, so there's no need to implement one separately — this is what you want for a full peripheral role.

## Reliability Considerations on Android

Android BLE is notoriously fragmented. According to Punch Through's 2025 Android BLE guide:
- Android 13 broke BLE for many users — a notable bug report on "Android 13: Unable to reconnect reliably to bonded peripheral" was assigned P1/S1 priority and resulted in a fix in Android 13 QPR1, while other issues like reading values from encrypted GATT characteristics and status 133 errors upon bonding are still being worked on
- Always assume that any operation has a nonzero probability of failing, and the app needs to be able to handle those failures. Even a simple disconnect and reconnect behind the scenes would solve most problems

Older library `flutter_ble_lib` is generally not recommended — flutter_BLE_lib often fails on fast concurrent writes and completes the future responsible for connecting to the device a bit too early.

## Recommendation Summary

For a **reliable Flutter BLE GATT server (peripheral) on Android in 2025**, the strongest options are:
1. **`bluetooth_low_energy`** — endorsed by the flutter_blue_plus maintainer, supports both central and peripheral roles
2. **`ble_peripheral`** — OS-independent, focused specifically on GATT server creation
3. **`flutter_ble_peripheral`** — also explicitly endorsed for the peripheral role

Pair whichever you choose with robust error handling and reconnection logic, since Android BLE stack issues persist regardless of which Flutter wrapper you use.

# Cardio App

A Flutter heart health companion app with real-time 3-lead ECG monitoring, AI-powered cardiac classification, and fall detection.

## Tech Stack
- Flutter (Dart SDK >=3.10.8 <4.0.0)
- Firebase Core, Firebase Auth, Cloud Firestore
- Running on **Android** (BLE requires native platform)
- Firebase project: `cardio-app-d4c55`
- fl_chart: ^0.70.2 (real-time ECG waveform visualization)
- flutter_blue_plus: ^1.35.0 (BLE communication with ESP32)
- permission_handler: ^11.0.0 (runtime BLE/location permissions)
- google_sign_in: ^6.2.1 (Google OAuth sign-in)
- tflite_flutter: ^0.12.1 (on-device AI inference for ECG + fall detection)
- flutter_local_notifications: ^19.0.0 (push alerts for abnormal ECG)
- google_fonts: ^6.0.0 (Inter font)
- shared_preferences: ^2.3.0 (local alert history)

## Hardware
- **Device**: ESP32 microcontroller
- **ECG**: 3-lead ECG module (e.g., AD8232) on PCB
- **Connection**: BLE (Bluetooth Low Energy)
- **Output**: JSON over BLE notifications
- **Sampling Rate**: ~250 Hz
- **ADC Resolution**: 12-bit (0-4095)

## Project Structure
```

├── main.dart                     # Firebase init + dark theme + MaterialApp
├── firebase_options.dart         # FlutterFire CLI generated
├── core/
│   ├── app_shell.dart            # Bottom nav (Monitor, History, Profile) + service ownership
│   └── splash_screen.dart        # Animated splash → auth check → routing
└── features/
    ├── auth/
    │   ├── data/

    │   │   └── user_model.dart          # UserModel with profile fields
    │   └── presentation/
    │       ├── login_page.dart
    │       ├── signup_page.dart
    │       └── forgot_password_page.dart
    ├── bluetooth/
    │   └── data/

    │       ├── ecg_data_model.dart       # EcgSample (3 ADC values) + EcgPrediction (5-class)
    │       └── sensor_data_model.dart    # SensorData + Vec3 (for fall detection BLE data)
```

## Architecture Decisions
- **Feature-based folder structure**: each feature has `data/` and `presentation/` subdirectories
- **AppShell** owns all shared services (BLE, ECG inference, notifications, history) and passes them to child pages
- **3-tab bottom nav**: Monitor (ECG), History (alerts), Profile (settings)
- **AuthService** centralizes all Firebase Auth + Firestore calls — pages don't call Firebase directly
- **Google Sign-In (OAuth)**: creates Firebase credential + auto-creates Firestore profile
- **BLE-only** — Classic Bluetooth was removed; uses flutter_blue_plus exclusively
- **Two AI models**: ECG classifier (5-class cardiac) + Fall detector (binary)
- **On-Device AI**: Both TFLite models run inside Flutter, NOT on ESP32
- **State management**: StatefulWidget + broadcast streams (no external state library)
- **Service injection**: prop drilling from AppShell to children

## BLE / ECG Integration
- ESP32 device name: `ECG_ESP32`
- BLE Service UUID: `12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789abc`
- BLE Characteristic UUID: `12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789abd`
- JSON batch format: `{"samples": [{"I": 2048, "II": 2100, "III": 1950}, ...]}`
- Brace-counting parser for robustness with fragmented BLE packets
- Leads-off detection: ADC values < 0 are filtered out
- Auto-reconnect on disconnect (3-second delay)
- Streams: `ecgStream` (List<EcgSample>), `connectionStream` (bool), `scanStream` (bool)

## ECG AI Pipeline
1. **Training**: PTB-XL dataset → extract 3 leads → preprocess → train in Colab
2. **Export**: PyTorch → ONNX → TFLite (float16 quantized, ~746 KB)
3. **Inference**: ECG samples → EcgProcessor (ADC→mV, baseline removal, z-score) → ring buffer (1250 samples, 3 leads) → TFLite → softmax → EMA smooth (alpha=0.3)
4. **Stride**: 250 samples (1 second) between inferences
5. **Notifications**: Local push on abnormal detection (confidence > 0.55, 30-sec cooldown per class)

## ECG Classification Classes
| Class | Full Name              | Color   |
|-------|------------------------|---------|
| NORM  | Normal ECG             | Green   |
| MI    | Myocardial Infarction  | Red     |
| STTC  | ST/T Change            | Orange  |
| CD    | Conduction Disturbance | Blue    |
| HYP   | Hypertrophy            | Purple  |

## Fall Detection (TFLite CNN)
- **Model**: Residual CNN trained on BITS-2 wrist-worn sensor dataset
- **Model file**: `assets/fall_detection.tflite` (~656 KB)
- **Input**: 128 timesteps x 12 features (9 raw sensor axes + 3 computed magnitudes)
- **Feature order**: `[acc_x, acc_y, acc_z, acg_x, acg_y, acg_z, gyro_x, gyro_y, gyro_z, acc_mag, acg_mag, gyro_mag]`
- **Normalization**: z-score with hardcoded mean/std from training (in `fall_detection_service.dart` and `ai/model_metadata.json`)
- **Sliding window**: 128 samples, step 64 (50% overlap), ~50 Hz sample rate
- **Threshold**: 0.5 probability — requires 2 consecutive windows above threshold in production
- **Test page**: Standalone `fall_test_page.dart` with 40 pre-extracted test windows (20 fall, 20 ADL)
- **Test data generation**: `ai/generate_test_cases.py` — must use EXACT same CSV parsing as training notebook (`load_and_clean_csv` with sensor pivot alignment)
- **Known**: Model v3 reports 84% sensitivity / 92% specificity on full test set
- **v4 notebook**: `ai/fall_detection_training_v4.ipynb` — improved version with SE attention, enhanced augmentation (rotation, drift, combined), adaptive labeling, cosine annealing LR, label smoothing

## Theme / Design
- **Dark theme** with Material3 (`ThemeMode.dark`)
- Background: `#0D1B2A` (near black), Surface: `#1A2332` (dark blue-gray)
- Accents: tealAccent primary + `#00BFA5` secondary
- Typography: Google Fonts (Inter)
- ECG charts: Lead I (red), Lead II (green), Lead III (blue)
- AI prediction card: color-coded by classification class
- Auth pages: teal gradient background + white text/inputs

## Navigation
```
SplashScreen (3 sec animation)
  ├→ No user → LoginPage (email/password + Google OAuth)
  └→ User exists → AppShell
                      ├── Tab 0: ECG Monitor (real-time charts + AI)
                      ├── Tab 1: History (alert log)
                      └── Tab 2: Profile (settings + sign out)
```

## Android Configuration
- minSdkVersion: 21
- Java/Kotlin: VERSION_17
- Core library desugaring enabled (`desugar_jdk_libs 2.1.4`)
- ProGuard rules for TFLite GPU delegate (`android/app/proguard-rules.pro`)
- Permissions: BLUETOOTH, BLUETOOTH_SCAN, BLUETOOTH_CONNECT, ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION

## Known Issues / Notes
- Firebase init in main.dart is wrapped in try-catch (Linux throws UnsupportedError)
- `AnimatedBuilder` is the correct Flutter widget name used in splash_screen.dart
- `sensor_data_model.dart` exists for fall detection BLE data (Vec3 accelerometer/gyroscope) — separate from ECG data model
- Fall detection test cases must be regenerated with `ai/generate_test_cases.py` if the dataset or model changes — the script uses the exact same CSV alignment as the training notebook
- ECG model must be placed at `assets/models/ecg_model.tflite`; fall model at `assets/fall_detection.tflite`
- Training code in `ecg_ml/` and `ai/` is for Google Colab — not compiled into the Flutter app
- `AuthService.createMissingProfile()` auto-creates Firestore doc for legacy users
- Notification cooldown: 30 seconds per ECG class to prevent spam

content.text: Pattern switching does mutate `_currentPattern`, and `_generateSample` reads it on every call. So the broadcast does change. Let me check tachycardia case — the switch in `_generateSample`:

Yes, the tester does broadcast different patterns — `_currentPattern` is read live every sample, and `BlePeripheral.updateCharacteristic` pushes immediately. The receiver gets the new shape within ~80ms (one packet).

But here's why your eye can't tell them apart — the patterns are differentiated only on **paper**, not in practice:

1. **Amplitudes are tiny vs. baseline drift.** All the wave components are 0.02–0.12 (P=0.02, QRS=0.05, T=0.06). After `(2048 + val*1000)` they only nudge ADC by 20–120 counts out of 4095 — almost flat lines after auto-scale. The QRS isn't biphasic either (no negative Q or S deflection), so it looks like a small bump, not the classic spike.

2. **The pattern-distinguishing features are subtle by design.** 
   - **MI**: adds an `ST elevation` Gaussian of amplitude 0.08 — same order as the T wave. Visually it just thickens the bump.
   - **HeartFailure**: scales Lead II by ×0.4 and Lead I by ×0.3, plus HR drops from 75→55. The shape is identical, just smaller and slower. On a 500-sample / 2-second window with auto-rescaling Y, the smaller amplitude is invisible — auto-scale stretches it back to fill the chart.
   - **Conduction**: only widens QRS from 0.05 to 0.12 (~60ms→~140ms). Real LBBB looks dramatic; here it's a slightly wider blob.
   - **Tachycardia**: same shape, HR 75→140. Auto-scaled X (sample index, not time) means you just see roughly twice as many beats packed in — easy to miss if you're not counting peaks.
   - **Noisy**: adds ±0.2 jitter, so this one IS visibly different.

3. **Auto-scaling Y axis hides amplitude differences entirely.** Your `_buildChart` recomputes `minY/maxY` from current data on every rebuild. Heart-failure's 30–40% lower amplitude gets re-stretched to fill the same 120px chart height as Normal. The only patterns that look different are Tachycardia (beat density) and Noisy (jitter).

4. **Lead III is computed (`leadII - leadI`), so it tracks the others.** No independent variation.

So: yes, the tester is broadcasting different data — but the patterns are **too similar in shape and amplitude**, and the receiver's **auto-Y-scaling erases the amplitude cue**, so they look nearly identical to the eye. The AI model would still see the differences (it normalizes per-window too, but uses the morphology).

If you want to verify: connect, switch to **Noisy** — that one you'll definitely see. If you want the others to be visually distinguishable too, the tester would need bigger amplitudes, real biphasic QRS, and stronger pattern-specific deformations (ST elevation 3–5× bigger, much wider QRS for conduction, etc.).

Analyzed both halves. Here's the truth — there are **multiple reasons no alarm is firing**, all visible in the code:

**1. The model probably isn't even being run on real data.**

`EcgProcessor._buffer` is initialized to **1250 zeros**. `isReady` becomes true as soon as `_sampleCount >= 1250 && samplesSinceLastInference >= 250`. Crucially, `_sampleCount` increments on every sample — but the buffer is *pre-filled with zeros*, so for the first ~5 seconds the model is doing inference on a buffer that's mostly zeros plus a few real samples at the tail end. Garbage in → garbage out, smoothed by EMA, so for the first ~5–10 seconds the model is locked on whatever class wins on a zero-input. That's almost certainly NORM (or stays uniform-ish). 

Then after `reset()` (called on disconnect or BLE toggle), it does `_buffer[ch] = List.filled(windowSize, 0.0)` — that's **fixed-length again**, so the next `removeAt(0)` will throw and silently kill inference (same bug we just fixed in initialization, but `reset` re-introduces it).

**2. Even on real data, the synthetic ECG doesn't look like PTB-XL.**

The model was trained on PTB-XL (real adult clinical 12-lead ECGs at 100 Hz, with all the morphology of real signal). The tester generates Gaussian-shaped P/QRS/T peaks with no Q wave, no S wave, no negative deflections — the QRS is a single positive bump 50ms wide. After baseline removal + z-score normalization, this looks like nothing the model has ever seen. Its output is undefined behavior — it'll lock onto whichever of NORM/MI/STTC/CD/HYP gets the highest spurious activation, but with low confidence and EMA smoothing keeping it stable.

**3. The amplitude is wrong by a factor of ~10.**

Tester: `2048 + val*1000` where val ≤ 1.0, then `toMillivolts` produces ≈ 800 mV peak QRS. Real ECG peaks are ~1–2 mV. After z-score normalization the *shape* is what matters, not absolute scale, so this part doesn't necessarily kill it — but combined with the alien morphology, the model is far off-distribution.

**4. The alert pipeline itself looks correct, but it's gated.**

`checkAndNotify` requires:
- `prediction.isNormal == false` (predicted class ≠ NORM)
- `prediction.confidence > 0.55`
- not in 30-second cooldown
- `_enabled && _initialized`
- Android notification permission granted

If the model is locked on NORM because of the buffer-of-zeros bootstrap problem, OR if it predicts an abnormal class but with confidence <0.55 (very likely given the garbage input), no alert ever fires. The pulse animation and history save are also gated on `prediction.isAbnormal` (`!isNormal && confidence > 0.5`).

**5. There's no "pattern → expected class" mapping anyway.**

Even if everything worked perfectly: switching the tester to "heart failure" doesn't mean the model should output HYP or anything specific. Heart failure isn't even one of the 5 classes (NORM/MI/STTC/CD/HYP). The closest analog would be HYP. The synthetic "heart failure" pattern (smaller amplitude) wouldn't reliably trigger HYP on a model trained on real LVH/RVH morphology.

- Try the **MI** pattern instead of heart failure — its shape (added ST elevation Gaussian) is the closest the tester gets to a real morphology change. If MI doesn't trigger an MI alert either, the model is definitively confused by the synthetic input.

**Bottom line:** the alarm pipeline is wired up correctly, but the synthetic ECG from the tester is too far from the model's training distribution to produce reliable predictions, AND the buffer-of-zeros bootstrap means the first inference window is contaminated, AND `reset()` reintroduces the fixed-length-list bug. # Make AI alarm fire on Heart-Failure tester pattern

## Context

The cardio_app's TFLite model is a 5-class classifier (NORM, MI, STTC, CD, HYP) trained on PTB-XL. **Heart Failure is not a native class** — clinically it co-presents with HYP (hypertrophy / ventricular remodeling) or CD (conduction disturbance / LBBB), so a working pipeline should fire an HYP or CD alert on heart-failure input.

Currently no alarm fires on any tester pattern, for three reasons:

1. **Synthetic input is far off-distribution.** The tester generates Gaussian-shaped P/QRS/T peaks with no Q wave, no S wave, no negative deflection, peak amplitude after `2048 + val*1000` of only ±0.1 ADC counts above midpoint after z-score. PTB-XL trained the model on real adult 12-lead recordings; nothing in the synthetic shape resembles training morphology, so the model's softmax stays near uniform and confidence never crosses 0.55.
2. **Buffer-of-zeros bootstrap.** `EcgProcessor._buffer` is pre-filled with 1250 zeros. As soon as `_sampleCount >= 1250` (after only ~5s of samples), inference runs on a buffer that is ~mostly zeros + a few tail samples. EMA smoothing locks the predicted class on whatever wins on near-zero input.
3. **`reset()` re-introduces the fixed-length-list bug we already fixed in initialization.** On disconnect/reconnect, `_buffer[ch] = List.filled(windowSize, 0.0)` returns a fixed-length list; the next `removeAt(0)` throws and silently kills inference.

The user accepted: **rewrite tester morphology to be ECG-realistic** (so the existing model recognizes patterns) and **keep model labels honest** (alert says "Hypertrophy Detected" on heartFailure input — that is what the model actually detects).

## Approach

### A. Tester (`C:\Users\islam\ecg_tester\lib\main.dart`) — rewrite `_generateSample`

Goal: generate biologically plausible 3-lead ECG morphology so the PTB-XL-trained model can classify it. Each pattern's deformation must shift the model to the intended target class.

**New per-sample model (per-beat, parameterized):**

For each beat at phase φ ∈ [0, 1) within `beatInterval = 60/HR`, build Lead II as:

```
P  =  0.10 mV  Gaussian(φ, 0.10, 0.025)
Q  = -0.08 mV  Gaussian(φ, 0.18, 0.010)
R  =  1.40 mV  Gaussian(φ, 0.20, 0.012)
S  = -0.30 mV  Gaussian(φ, 0.22, 0.012)
T  =  0.30 mV  Gaussian(φ, 0.40, 0.060)
```

Lead I: `0.5 * R + 0.6 * P + 0.7 * T + 0.6 * Q` (smaller R, similar shape).
Lead III: `leadII − leadI` (Einthoven's law).

Pattern-specific deformations:

- **normal** — baseline morphology above; 75 bpm.
- **mi** — add **ST elevation** plateau between J-point and T (`+0.4 mV` flat across φ ∈ [0.24, 0.34]) + **inverted T wave** (T amplitude × −0.5). 75 bpm. Aim: model fires MI.
- **heartFailure** — emulate LVH morphology common in HF: **R amplitude × 2.5** (so ~3.5 mV in lead II), **wider QRS** (S Gaussian width × 2), **inverted T wave** (T × −0.7), HR 55. Strain pattern + tall R = HYP. Aim: model fires HYP (or CD as secondary).
- **conduction** — wide QRS only: Q/R/S Gaussian widths × 3, peak amplitudes × 1.2 to keep area roughly constant. 75 bpm. Aim: model fires CD.
- **tachycardia** — same as normal, HR 140. Aim: probably stays NORM — that's correct behavior, the tester just speeds up sinus.
- **noisy** — normal + uniform noise ±0.4 mV per sample on all leads. Aim: low-confidence predictions, no alert.
- **leadsOff** — unchanged: returns [-1, -1, -1].

Critical: bump amplitude from `val * 1000` ADC counts to a proper full-scale mapping. Real ECG peak ≈ 1.5 mV; ADC midpoint = 2048; range = ±1650 mV at vref=3.3V. So `toAdc(val_mV) = (2048 + val_mV * (4095 / 3300)).clamp(0, 4094).toInt()` — this puts a 1.4mV R wave at ADC≈3787, comfortably within 12-bit range.

### B. EcgProcessor (`C:\Users\islam\Hinvest\cardio_app\lib\features\ecg\data\ecg_processor.dart`)

Two fixes:

1. **Don't run inference on the bootstrap buffer.** Replace the current `isReady` rule so it requires `_sampleCount >= windowSize` based on **real samples received**, not the pre-filled zeros. The pre-filled buffer makes the first inference window 100% real samples by sample 1250 — that's already correct, but only because we're shifting in real samples and shifting out zeros. Wait — re-checking: at sample N (≤1250), buffer is `[0]*((1250-N)) ++ realSamples[0..N]`. At N=1250 the window is fully real. So `_sampleCount >= 1250` correctly waits until full. **No change needed here** — but document it.
2. **Fix `reset()`** to produce a growable list:
   ```dart

   ```

- `EcgInferenceService._runInference` runs softmax + EMA(α=0.3) → emits `EcgPrediction`.
- `_onPrediction` in `ecg_monitor_page.dart` calls `widget.notificationService.checkAndNotify(prediction)`.

  - `!prediction.isNormal` → predicted class ≠ NORM
  - `prediction.confidence > 0.55`

2. `C:\Users\islam\Hinvest\cardio_app\lib\features\ecg\data\ecg_processor.dart` — fix `reset()` to create a growable list.

# Cardio App

A Flutter heart health companion app with real-time 3-lead ECG monitoring, AI-powered cardiac classification, and fall detection.

## Tech Stack
- Flutter (Dart SDK >=3.10.8 <4.0.0)
- Firebase Core, Firebase Auth, Cloud Firestore
- Running on **Android** (BLE requires native platform)
- Firebase project: `cardio-app-d4c55`
- fl_chart: ^0.70.2 (real-time ECG waveform visualization)
- flutter_blue_plus: ^1.35.0 (BLE communication with ESP32)
- permission_handler: ^11.0.0 (runtime BLE/location permissions)
- google_sign_in: ^6.2.1 (Google OAuth sign-in)
- tflite_flutter: ^0.12.1 (on-device AI inference for ECG + fall detection)
- flutter_local_notifications: ^19.0.0 (push alerts for abnormal ECG)
- google_fonts: ^6.0.0 (Inter font)
